corrected_value.title: Genetic imaging of the association of oxytocin receptor gene (OXTR) polymorphisms with positive maternal parenting

decision.location: Discussion, lines 309-318 (see also Abstract, lines 13-17; Introduction, lines 93-108; Works Cited, lines 517-518)
decision.quote:
The current study investigated the association between child and parent OXTR genotype ( OXTR rs53576) and observed
parental warmth, control, and negativity in both mothers and fathers in a
population-based sample of 500 families with twin children between the ages of 6 and
10, in an attempt to replicate and extend prior research ( Bakermans-Kranenburg & van IJzendoorn, 2008 ; Michalska et al., 2014 ). Although only
preliminary given the sample size, our results revealed a significant association
between maternal OXTR rs53576 genotype and warmth, even when
controlling for the effects of child age, gender, and ethnicity, as well as
child-driven evocative effects. This finding not only serves as a constructive
replication of previous research examining the relationship between variants within OXTR and parenting ( Bakermans-Kranenburg & van IJzendoorn, 2008 ; Feldman et al., 2012 ; Michalska et al., 2014 ), but also adds to the growing body of research
supporting a link between oxytocin functioning and parenting ( Feldman et al., 2012 ; Weisman, Zagoory-Sharon, & Feldman, 2012 ).
decision.reason: The study empirically tested the association between OXTR rs53576 genotype and observed parenting in 500 twin families and explicitly states in the Abstract, Introduction, and Discussion that it was conducted to constructively replicate and extend Michalska et al. (2014), which examined OXTR rs53576 and observed positive maternal parenting in 40 mothers. The Works Cited section confirms the exact identity: Michalska KJ, Decety J, Liu C, Chen Q, Martz ME, Jacob S, Lahey BB (2014), 'Genetic imaging of the association of oxytocin receptor gene (OXTR) polymorphisms with positive maternal parenting', Frontiers in Behavioral Neuroscience 8:21, DOI 10.3389/fnbeh.2014.00021. It is completely distinct from shipped row 9 (Bakermans-Kranenburg & van IJzendoorn, 2008; 10.1093/scan/nsn004) and sibling target 2 (Feldman et al., 2012; 10.1016/j.biopsych.2011.12.025). Prior adjudication and state files were checked and are legitimately absent.
